sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 2009. Penultimate lengthening in Bantu; Hyman 2017. Bantu tone overview (UC Berkeley PhonLab Annual Reports); Downing 2004 ZASPiL 37 accent typology (already on file under haya1250).
sources.note: Grepped for Khayo/Luyia: no Khayo entry; only Saamia and Bukusu mentioned in Hyman 2017 for tone. No second-hand stress statement for Khayo.

sources.citation: Marlo, Michael R. 2009. Khayo verbal tonology. Africana Linguistica 15: 77-129. DOI 10.3406/aflin.2009.1003 (Persée).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey); publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 'Overview of tone in Khayo' (p.79): one underlying tone H vs. toneless, mora is the TBU, contours on long vowels, automatic downstep, 'predictable' tone system without lexical tone contrast in verb roots, melodic Hs mark TAMP; p.93: no phrase-medial vs. phrase-final tonal alternations; p.106: Flop (H final->penult mora in disyllabic stems) is stem/word-final, not phrase-final. The word 'stress' never occurs; 'accent' only in reference titles; no mention of penultimate lengthening.

sources.citation: Marlo, Michael R. 2008. Tura verbal tonology. Studies in African Linguistics 37(2): 153-243.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2 (pp.155-156): Tura (neighbouring Luyia variety, filed under khay1238 by Glottolog) has a privative H vs. toneless system, L is default, contours on long vowels, phrase-final H realized phonetically falling; verbal tone 'most similar to Khayo, Nyala-West, Saamia, Songa'.

sources.citation: Osotsi, Eric Mbeya. 2020. A systematic reconstruction of the phonology of Proto-Luyia: a comparative analysis. MA project, University of Nairobi. 127 pp. (hdl 11295/154048)
sources.note: Nothing; segmental reconstruction only; lists Khayo [JE341] among Luyia dialects; no prosody.

sources.citation: Etakwa, Everlyn. 2019. The phonology of Olutura syllables. PhD thesis, University of Nairobi. 312 pp. (hdl 11295/108688)
sources.note: Nothing; segment inventory, contrastive vowel length, syllable structure of Tura; explicitly states it 'did not deal with other aspects of Olutura supra-segmental phonology such as tone'. Cites Kebeya, Bwire & Erastus 2016 on Lukhayo intra-dialectal segmental variation.
